pathway.title: IRON MOUNTAIN INC — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: IRON MOUNTAIN INC carries total debt of USD 17,972.2 million at September 30, 2026, which is 6.22x LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,888.2 million and 6.16x on a net basis, compared with 6.38x and 6.32x at FY2025. Leverage fell against FY2025 because Adjusted EBITDA grew faster than debt, but it rose slightly from 6.19x at LTM Q2 2026, and a stricter measure that does not add back stock-based compensation, restructuring or acquisition costs (operating income plus depreciation and amortization) gives 6.81x. Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure that adds back items such as stock-based compensation, so the headline ratios understate leverage on a stricter basis.

The company does not fund its investment programme from operations. Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of USD 1,203.6 million was below capex of USD 1,724.2 million, a shortfall of USD 520.6 million before USD 790.0 million of dividends. Debt rose from USD 16,432.0 million at December 31, 2025, and the cash flow statement shows senior note proceeds and noncontrolling interest contributions as sources. Data center growth capex dominates the spending, so the credit improves only as leased capacity commences and converts to revenue.

Liquidity is ample but moving down. Cash of USD 188.2 million and revolver availability of USD 2,218.2 million give USD 2,406.4 million, against USD 2,912.4 million at June 30, 2026, because revolver borrowings rose by USD 489.5 million in Q3 2026. Interest cover is steady: Adjusted EBITDA is 3.16x cash interest paid on an LTM basis against 3.12x at FY2025, and the weighted average interest rate is 5.7%.

Near-term refinancing is the main event risk. The current portion of long-term debt is USD 1,232.9 million, which includes the USD 1,000.0 million 4 7/8% notes due September 15, 2027. The last company-printed maturity table (December 31, 2025) shows USD 2,330.8 million due in 2027, USD 1,663.7 million in 2028, USD 2,137.5 million in 2029 and USD 3,035.7 million in 2030; some of that has since been extended or refinanced, but no later table is printed. The Credit Agreement tests show 4.8x lease adjusted leverage against a 7.0x maximum and 2.5x fixed charge coverage against a 1.5x minimum, so reported headroom is wide, although those ratios use other definitions than Adjusted EBITDA and cannot be rebuilt from the sources.

On the business side, Global RIM generated USD 5,291.5 million of revenue and USD 2,363.5 million of segment Adjusted EBITDA in FY2025, and nine-month 2026 data center revenue was USD 791.2 million, up 39.6%. Management reports leasing of 137 megawatts year to date, which is signed capacity, not commenced revenue. The board raised the quarterly dividend by 15% to USD 0.993 per share on November 5, 2026, and the indentures do not treat a leveraged recapitalization as a change of control, so event protection for noteholders is limited. No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed, which removes sponsor extraction as a driver but also leaves ownership unassessed.

runs.text: Strengths. The recurring storage base is the first strength: Global RIM contributes most segment profit, management states a majority of revenue is recurring, storage contracts run one to five years and no customer exceeds about 3% of revenue, so cash flow is not exposed to a single name. The data center segment is a second strength, because long leases with a weighted average expiration of 10.3 years at December 31, 2025 and a segment margin that rose to 53.6% give visibility on a growing earnings layer. Third, reported covenant headroom is wide and the revolver, which matures in 2030, has USD 2,218.2 million available, which supports liquidity for the next twelve months despite near-term maturities. Fourth, funding is diversified across notes, bank debt, project loans and a receivables program, and the 2026 issuance extended the note stack to 2035. All are tagged Documentary Fact except the recurring-revenue share and the leasing pace, which are Management Language.

Weaknesses. Leverage of 6.22x on a management EBITDA measure, and 6.81x on a stricter measure, leaves limited tolerance for an earnings shortfall. Free cash flow is negative before dividends and the company has raised its dividend while borrowing, so debt rises each year while the data center build runs; the REIT distribution rules and a stated commitment to dividend growth increase financing needs. Refinancing exposure is concentrated in 2027 to 2030. Project debt and a new joint venture add structurally senior and noncontrolling claims at subsidiaries that sit ahead of parent noteholders, and the parent notes depend on subsidiary guarantors and cash upstream. The ALM business relies on a limited number of clients and China-based buyers, and Corporate and Other carries negative segment Adjusted EBITDA after corporate costs. Ownership, contract backlog and ratings are not supplied, which limits the assessment of business risk; missing evidence is not treated as adverse.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: There is no sponsor transaction, leveraged buyout or change of control in the sources, so the transaction view is the set of financing and investment events in the period. All items below are completed unless stated, and each is a Documentary Fact from the cited filing.

In Q2 2026, on June 26, 2026, IMI completed a private offering of 1,500,000 thousand of 6 1/4% Notes due 2035, issued at par with a maturity of January 15, 2035, interest paid January 15 and July 15 and a par call date of July 15, 2031; net proceeds of about 1,481,800 thousand repaid part of the revolving credit facility borrowings and funded general corporate purposes (10-Q Q3 page:22-23). The Q2 2026 quarterly report prints the par call date as July 15, 2031 in its debt note (10-Q Q2 page:21) and as July 15, 2029 in its MD&A table (10-Q Q2 page:47); both spans are quoted in the conflicts table and the conflict is logged, not reconciled. In Q1 2026, on January 9, 2026, two wholly-owned subsidiaries entered into mortgage and mezzanine loans with a total original principal of 433,000 thousand (Virginia 3 Term Loans due 2031, maturing January 9, 2031, weighted average rate 6.3%), used to repay the earlier Virginia 3 loans and part of the revolver (10-Q Q3 page:21). On June 9, 2026, Iron Mountain Data Centers Virginia 9, LLC entered into a credit agreement allowing term loans up to 298,000 thousand at SOFR plus 3.00%, maturing June 9, 2029 with two one-year extension options, with 138,627 thousand outstanding at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:21-22). In the same quarter the company formed Iron Mountain Data Centers Virginia 9 JV, LP with an unnamed partner, creating initial noncontrolling interests of about 49,900 thousand (10-Q Q3 page:24). On May 28, 2026 the receivables securitization program was amended to include certain Canadian entities, increase capacity from 400,000 thousand to 450,000 thousand and extend maturity from July 1, 2027 to July 1, 2029 (10-Q Q3 page:22).

Other items in the period: a finance lease expected to commence in the fourth quarter of 2026 with a 31-year term and about 223,400 thousand of undiscounted minimum payments (10-Q Q3 page:10); acquisitions in the ALM business, with cash paid for acquisitions of 8,033 thousand in nine months 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:6) and a 31.7 million increase in Corporate and Other service revenue attributed to acquisitions (10-Q Q3 page:44); and the deferred purchase obligation for the 2024 Regency Technologies acquisition, which has an earnout of up to 200,000 thousand payable in 2027 if earned and a fair value of 210,188 thousand at September 30, 2026 (10-K page:134; 10-Q Q3 page:10-11). The creditor effect is that the 2026 issuance extended the bond stack to 2035 and moved some bank borrowing into fixed rate notes, while project debt at subsidiaries and a new joint venture add structurally senior and noncontrolling claims; the stated use of proceeds was repayment of existing revolver borrowings, which in my reading restored revolver capacity rather than adding committed liquidity (Analyst Interpretation). Subsequent events up to the cutoff: the board declared a dividend of 0.993 per share on November 5, 2026, payable January 6, 2027 to holders of record on December 15, 2026, and management raised full-year 2026 guidance; both are subsequent to the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and are not folded into period facts (10-Q Q3 page:24; Release Q3 page:2). No new debt issue after September 30, 2026 appears in the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: IRON MOUNTAIN INC is a listed US real estate investment trust with no sponsor or controlling owner disclosed in the pinned sources. Its credit rests on three operating blocks that behave differently. Global RIM (records management, data management, digital solutions, shredding, media and consumer storage) is the recurring core: FY2025 segment revenue was 5,291,481 thousand and segment Adjusted EBITDA 2,363,498 thousand. Management says a majority of revenue is recurring, storage contracts run one to five years and no customer exceeds about 3% of revenue; all three are management or filing statements and the sources give no volume data beyond stating that volume is expected to be relatively stable, so growth in this segment comes from revenue management (pricing). Global Data Center is the growth engine: FY2025 revenue 803,429 thousand, Adjusted EBITDA 416,326 thousand, with nine-month 2026 revenue up 39.6% on lease commencements. It also absorbs most of the capital: nine-month 2026 data center growth capex was 1,344,097 thousand of 1,589,574 thousand total growth capex. Corporate and Other (ALM, Fine Arts and corporate costs) grew revenue 55.9% in nine months 2026 partly through acquisitions and reports negative segment Adjusted EBITDA (109,611 thousand loss) because corporate costs sit in it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For a creditor the transmission mechanism is: recurring storage cash flow plus long data center leases (weighted average lease expiration 10.3 years at December 31, 2025) give revenue visibility; the same data center growth consumes cash ahead of revenue, so debt rose to 17,972,202 thousand while operating cash flow of 1,203,634 thousand trailed capex of 1,724,205 thousand (CP-1). The 2026 transactions were financings, not a change of control: a 1,500,000 thousand note issue, two data center project financings, a receivables program upsize and one new joint venture with an unnamed partner. The credit implication is refinancing and market-access dependence rather than sponsor or ownership risk, and the sources do not allow an ownership or sponsor-behaviour assessment beyond documented issuer actions. Governance of creditor-relevant behaviour is Neutral or Mixed: distributions are tied to REIT status and are rising while free cash flow is negative, but there is no documented priming, uptiering, drop-down or collateral release.

The Q2 2026 quarterly report prints the par call date as July 15, 2031 in its debt note (10-Q Q2 page:21) and as July 15, 2029 in its MD&A table (10-Q Q2 page:47); both spans are quoted in the conflicts table and the conflict is logged, not reconciled. In Q1 2026, on January 9, 2026, two wholly-owned subsidiaries entered into mortgage and mezzanine loans with a total original principal of 433,000 thousand (Virginia 3 Term Loans due 2031, maturing January 9, 2031, weighted average rate 6.3%), used to repay the earlier Virginia 3 loans and part of the revolver (10-Q Q3 page:21). On June 9, 2026, Iron Mountain Data Centers Virginia 9, LLC entered into a credit agreement allowing term loans up to 298,000 thousand at SOFR plus 3.00%, maturing June 9, 2029 with two one-year extension options, with 138,627 thousand outstanding at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:21-22). In the same quarter the company formed Iron Mountain Data Centers Virginia 9 JV, LP with an unnamed partner, creating initial noncontrolling interests of about 49,900 thousand (10-Q Q3 page:24). On May 28, 2026 the receivables securitization program was amended to include certain Canadian entities, increase capacity from 400,000 thousand to 450,000 thousand and extend maturity from July 1, 2027 to July 1, 2029 (10-Q Q3 page:22).

The creditor effect is that the 2026 issuance extended the bond stack to 2035 and moved some bank borrowing into fixed rate notes, while project debt at subsidiaries and a new joint venture add structurally senior and noncontrolling claims; the stated use of proceeds was repayment of existing revolver borrowings, which in my reading restored revolver capacity rather than adding committed liquidity (Analyst Interpretation). fields.value: IRON MOUNTAIN INC is a large, diversified and cash-generative REIT whose debt load, at 6.22x LTM Adjusted EBITDA, is high and still growing, so the credit view is cautious: sound operations on a stretched balance sheet. The strongest support is a recurring storage business with Global RIM revenue of USD 5,291.5 million and no customer above about 3%, plus a data center segment growing 39.6% with a 53.6% margin. The weakest point is that nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of USD 1,203.6 million fell short of capex of USD 1,724.2 million and dividends of USD 790.0 million. The outcome is decided by whether data center leases commence on schedule and whether the company keeps refinancing, including USD 1,000.0 million of notes due September 15, 2027, at acceptable cost. [Confidence: Medium; Analyst Interpretation.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: IRON MOUNTAIN INC carries total debt of USD 17,972.2 million at September 30, 2026, which is 6.22x LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,888.2 million and 6.16x on a net basis, compared with 6.38x and 6.32x at FY2025. Leverage fell against FY2025 because Adjusted EBITDA grew faster than debt, but it rose slightly from 6.19x at LTM Q2 2026, and a stricter measure that does not add back stock-based compensation, restructuring or acquisition costs (operating income plus depreciation and amortization) gives 6.81x. Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure that adds back items such as stock-based compensation, so the headline ratios understate leverage on a stricter basis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company does not fund its investment programme from operations. Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of USD 1,203.6 million was below capex of USD 1,724.2 million, a shortfall of USD 520.6 million before USD 790.0 million of dividends. Debt rose from USD 16,432.0 million at December 31, 2025, and the cash flow statement shows senior note proceeds and noncontrolling interest contributions as sources. Data center growth capex dominates the spending, so the credit improves only as leased capacity commences and converts to revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is ample but moving down. Cash of USD 188.2 million and revolver availability of USD 2,218.2 million give USD 2,406.4 million, against USD 2,912.4 million at June 30, 2026, because revolver borrowings rose by USD 489.5 million in Q3 2026. Interest cover is steady: Adjusted EBITDA is 3.16x cash interest paid on an LTM basis against 3.12x at FY2025, and the weighted average interest rate is 5.7%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Near-term refinancing is the main event risk. The current portion of long-term debt is USD 1,232.9 million, which includes the USD 1,000.0 million 4 7/8% notes due September 15, 2027. The last company-printed maturity table (December 31, 2025) shows USD 2,330.8 million due in 2027, USD 1,663.7 million in 2028, USD 2,137.5 million in 2029 and USD 3,035.7 million in 2030; some of that has since been extended or refinanced, but no later table is printed. The Credit Agreement tests show 4.8x lease adjusted leverage against a 7.0x maximum and 2.5x fixed charge coverage against a 1.5x minimum, so reported headroom is wide, although those ratios use other definitions than Adjusted EBITDA and cannot be rebuilt from the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the business side, Global RIM generated USD 5,291.5 million of revenue and USD 2,363.5 million of segment Adjusted EBITDA in FY2025, and nine-month 2026 data center revenue was USD 791.2 million, up 39.6%. Management reports leasing of 137 megawatts year to date, which is signed capacity, not commenced revenue. The board raised the quarterly dividend by 15% to USD 0.993 per share on November 5, 2026, and the indentures do not treat a leveraged recapitalization as a change of control, so event protection for noteholders is limited. No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed, which removes sponsor extraction as a driver but also leaves ownership unassessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. The recurring storage base is the first strength: Global RIM contributes most segment profit, management states a majority of revenue is recurring, storage contracts run one to five years and no customer exceeds about 3% of revenue, so cash flow is not exposed to a single name. The data center segment is a second strength, because long leases with a weighted average expiration of 10.3 years at December 31, 2025 and a segment margin that rose to 53.6% give visibility on a growing earnings layer. Third, reported covenant headroom is wide and the revolver, which matures in 2030, has USD 2,218.2 million available, which supports liquidity for the next twelve months despite near-term maturities. Fourth, funding is diversified across notes, bank debt, project loans and a receivables program, and the 2026 issuance extended the note stack to 2035. All are tagged Documentary Fact except the recurring-revenue share and the leasing pace, which are Management Language.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Leverage of 6.22x on a management EBITDA measure, and 6.81x on a stricter measure, leaves limited tolerance for an earnings shortfall. Free cash flow is negative before dividends and the company has raised its dividend while borrowing, so debt rises each year while the data center build runs; the REIT distribution rules and a stated commitment to dividend growth increase financing needs. Refinancing exposure is concentrated in 2027 to 2030. Project debt and a new joint venture add structurally senior and noncontrolling claims at subsidiaries that sit ahead of parent noteholders, and the parent notes depend on subsidiary guarantors and cash upstream. The ALM business relies on a limited number of clients and China-based buyers, and Corporate and Other carries negative segment Adjusted EBITDA after corporate costs. Ownership, contract backlog and ratings are not supplied, which limits the assessment of business risk; missing evidence is not treated as adverse.
